paragraph: In late December 2023 the security ministry's director of information systems told a delegation that its computerised main courante platform [was not yet operational](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2023/12/30/digital-burkina-faso-main-courante-informatisee-la-fin-du-papier-pour-les-forces-de-lordre/>). The digital transition ministry put it at more than 80 per cent built. The platform [is to replace the physical registers in which main courantes are kept at police commissariats and gendarmerie brigades](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2023/12/30/digital-burkina-faso-main-courante-informatisee-la-fin-du-papier-pour-les-forces-de-lordre/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated on or before 30 September 2026 says it went live in any commissariat or brigade, and no station count has been found. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

No stage is set. In June 2020 GIZ said the police had [a digitised system for investigations, criminal proceedings, arrest warrants, fines and sanctions](<https://www.giz.de/en/downloads/giz2020_fr_appui_a_la_police_camerounaise.pdf>). It also said the system was [barely used](<https://www.giz.de/en/downloads/giz2020_fr_appui_a_la_police_camerounaise.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found since 2020. No source found says which units use the system or whether any is outside the capital. Nor does any say how many stations enter records in it. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

On 15 March 2023 a human rights programme officer told Canada's Immigration and Refugee Board that a police statement [must by law be written out and signed by the officer who drafts it, on pain of nullity](<https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2092757.html>). In March 2023 the Executive Secretary of Héritiers de la justice told the board that police documents [are typed, and the record of the parties' hearings is handwritten in most cases](<https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2092757.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports a digital system for stations. Neither account says in terms that none exists. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

No stage is set. The one statement that stations work by hand is a survey of commissariats in Pointe-Noire and Nkayi from January 2014. Nothing has been found on Brazzaville, the rest of the country or the gendarmerie beyond one brigade, and nothing dated since. In the last twelve months, the [criminal-record extract in the first wave of state services to go online](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/le-numerique-au-service-dun-congo-plus-performant-plus-souverain-et-plus-proche-de-ses>) was planned in July 2026. Nothing has been found on who would own a station system. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

On 27 December 2024 two ministries issued an order [making use of the electronic criminal process obligatory in the Polícia Nacional](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/View/73167>). The Attorney General says the system [entered service in the Praia and São Vicente police districts](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=73434>) on 30 January 2025. In the last twelve months, on 16 March 2026 NOSi [formally handed the subsystem over](<https://justica.gov.cv/w/nosi-entrega-sistema-de-informa%C3%A7%C3%A3o-da-justi%C3%A7a-penal>) to the Ministry of Justice. No count or share of stations using it has been found. Operating would need more than half of stations entering reports or cases digitally, with a published share or count.

No stage is set. The one statement on stations dates from January 2021 and says they often lack the technology to write reports on a computer. It names no system, no place and no count of stations, and it does not say that stations record on paper only. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on who would own a station system. Absent would need a dated source stating that police stations record reports and cases on paper only.

Ethiopia's Ministry of Justice says [the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute is developing it](<https://justice.gov.et/en/news/development-of-technology-to-digitalize-the-criminal-justice-system-is-underway-officials-announced/>), its Criminal Records Information Management System, CRIMS. In August 2023 the ministry [was training federal investigating police and prosecutors, about 100 in all](<https://justice.gov.et/en/news/training-aimed-at-broadly-launching-the-case-record-information-management-system-crims-is-being-provided/>), to launch it widely. In the last twelve months, in January 2026 the ministry said the system [is under development and not yet in use](<https://justice.gov.et/en/news/development-of-technology-to-digitalize-the-criminal-justice-system-is-underway-officials-announced/>). No station or place has been found, and no launch since 2023. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

No stage is set. The only records system found is a vendor's design, presented at a Libreville seminar on 10 January 2026. No adoption by the police, the gendarmerie or a ministry is stated, and no station is shown using it. In the last twelve months, the gendarmerie's [Identity Secu](<https://ethiquemediagabon.net/?p=14508>) mobile application was deployed at the PK9 brigade in Libreville on 8 May 2026, as an application for the public. No dated statement says how stations record today, and no plan, finance or count of stations has been found. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

Ghana's Government [launched the Case Tracking System, as it calls it, in 2018 with USAID support](<https://www.newsghana.com.gh/more-training-needed-on-cts-police-superintendent/>), as a common platform for the police, the Attorney General's office and the Prisons Service. The Legal Resources Centre reported in 2022 that [55 police stations and 3 prisons services were using the system](<https://lrcghana.org/lets-resource-case-tracking-system-lrc/>), in seven regions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing on the system since 2022 has been found. No total of stations has been found to set beside the 55. Operating would need more than half of stations entering reports or cases digitally, with a published share or count.

No stage is set. An account dated 31 March 2021 says ten police and gendarmerie units of Greater Conakry were equipped. It gives no total of units, does not state that any entered records, and gives the digitising of procès-verbaux as an intention. A decree of 13 May 2019 created the police data centre and its information system, and names no station. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no dated statement says how stations record today. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted: staff trained, equipment delivered, an agreement signed or pilot stations using it.

At a media briefing reported on 24 March 2026 the Inspector General of Police [described the force's documentation as paper-based](<https://standard.gm/police-must-transition-from-paper-documentation-to-digitalised-mode-igp>). He said the force [needs to move from paper-based documentation to a digitalised mode](<https://standard.gm/police-must-transition-from-paper-documentation-to-digitalised-mode-igp>). UNDP's terms of reference of 22 April 2021 had described [a mobile app for crime reporting by police officers as in its pilot phase](<https://procurement-notices.undp.org/view_file.cfm?doc_id=251674>). In the last twelve months, the briefing is the only source found on how the force records. Nothing says what became of the app or how many stations took part. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

In August 2024 the author of an undergraduate project at IFBA stated that Guinea-Bissau [does not have a system for recording criminal occurrences in police stations](<https://ads.ifba.edu.br/dl2773>). The author cited no source. In the last twelve months, on 12 September 2025 INTERPOL described the West African Police Information System as [strengthening information exchange and coordination among the region's law enforcement agencies](<https://www.interpol.int/News-and-Events/News/2025/President-of-Guinea-Bissau-visits-INTERPOL-headquarters>). No station is named as entering its cases at the criminal-information centre in Bissau. Nothing has been found on how stations record, or on a plan. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

The National Police Service's annual report for 2022 says its Digital Occurrence Book was [launched at Kasarani Sub-County, Nairobi, on 21 November 2019](<http://www.nationalpolice.go.ke/sites/default/files/2024-10/ANNUAL%20REPORT%202022%20A4%20SIZE.pdf>). The Star reported that [76 police stations in and around Nairobi had digital Occurrence Books by 30 June 2023](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2023-07-03-76-police-occurrence-books-digitised-in-modernisation-drive>). In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the Uasin Gishu police commander said the [digital Occurrence Book had been rolled out at five Eldoret stations](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/counties/rift-valley/2026-03-12-eldoret-police-shift-to-digital-ob-system-to-boost-crime-reporting>). In May 2026 the Inspector General told MPs [the service did not yet have digital Occurrence Books](<https://www.capitalfm.co.ke/news/2026/05/police-turn-to-technology-cctv-and-body-cameras-to-secure-2027-polls/>). No source reconciles the two. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

UNDP reports that the crime statistics system [went live at police headquarters on 25 January 2021, with training for 15 personnel](<https://www.undp.org/liberia/news/national-police-online-crime-statistics-system-goes-live>). [Six officers were chosen to pioneer it in Montserrado County, the seat of the capital](<https://www.undp.org/liberia/stories/policewoman-breaks-digital-barrier-new-crime-statistics-and-information-system>), that month. UNDP also reported that a case management system [was up and running at the police in June 2022](<https://www.undp.org/liberia/blog/innovative-online-case-management-system-ushers-liberias-judiciary-digital-age>). In the last twelve months, FrontPageAfrica reported in 2026 that [Nyehn Town Police Station, the only police facility serving Todee District, has no computers](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/news/liberia-rural-security-at-risk-as-nyehn-town-police-station-falls-apart/>). No fact shows either system in use at a station outside Montserrado County. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

On 3 May 2025 Tripoli's security director told the heads of investigation of the police stations to attend to the running of the digital system. In the last twelve months, the directorate [inaugurated its digital transformation system, including the police-station investigation-reports system, on 31 December 2025](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=347992&lang=ar>). The Libyan News Agency reports that it serves the [police stations and traffic sections of the Tripoli Security Directorate](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=347992&lang=ar>). No station outside that directorate is shown using a records system. No count of stations, plan or finance has been found. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally in some stations outside the capital.

No stage is set. The Ombudsman's inspection, begun in July 2023, found posts without stationery keeping registers by hand. The Inspector of Police's report for 2024/25 describes a makeshift paper incident book at a station. Neither says that stations record on paper only. In the last twelve months, [20 desktop computers were handed to the police service](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/undp-lesotho_undplesotho-peacebuilding-digitaltransformation-activity-7471073069931941888-3nAP>) in June 2026, and the communications authority put a [Wi-Fi project for thirteen police stations](<https://lca.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/RFP-POLICE-STATIONS-WI-FI-PROJECT-31-JULY-2026_final-.pdf>) out for proposals in July 2026. No records system for stations has been found. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

Morocco's national police, the DGSN, [built GESTARR with its own technical staff](<https://lematin.ma/journal/2019/generalisation-systeme-informatique-gestion-arrondissements-police/320740.html>). Complaints lodged at arrondissements were managed in it in October 2019. In 2024 the DGSN [added a system for crime and misdemeanour cases at the arrondissements, each case followed through investigation to submission to the judicial authorities](<https://www.lereporter.ma/la-direction-generale-de-la-surete-nationale-presente-son-bilan-annuel-au-titre-de-lannee-2024/>). In the last twelve months, its review of 2025 says [Qadaya's rollout continued during the year](<https://www.lavieeco.com/pouvoirs/securite/la-dgsn-mise-sur-le-numerique-pour-rapprocher-ses-services-des-citoyens/>). It reached 16 of the 22 police commands. The DGSN counts commands, not stations, so no share of stations has been found. Operating would need more than half of stations entering reports or cases digitally, with a published share or count.

UNDP's evaluators visited stations and commands in September 2007 and verified [the almost complete absence of digital records of autos, case files or any other procedure across the force](<https://erc.undp.org/evaluation/documents/download/3514>). They found that the use of information technology [was non-existent at district and police station level](<https://erc.undp.org/evaluation/documents/download/3514>). On 23 August 2024 Club of Mozambique reported [a public security management information system for the Ministry of the Interior](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-to-have-a-public-security-management-information-system-watch/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fact says that stations enter reports or cases in that system. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

The central office for collecting police information [supervises the police information system](<https://mourassiloun.com/node/36165>), which the General Directorate of National Security calls WAPIS. The system was launched on 19 June 2025. At the launch the director of the central office [gave the centres linked as 27 of the National Police and 7 of the National Gendarmerie](<https://mourassiloun.com/node/36165>). The report puts the rollout across Nouakchott's commissariats at 90 per cent complete. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source shows the system in use at a station outside Nouakchott, and no total of stations has been found. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

The Prime Minister told the National Assembly on 17 June 2025 that the Crime Occurrence Tracking System [manages and tracks complaints and declarations from initial reporting to final case disposal](<https://mauritiusassembly.govmu.org/mauritiusassembly/index.php/download/472/2025/23646/debate-no-16-of-2025-unrevised-tuesday-17-june-2025.pdf>). He said [all police stations are equipped with personal computers for the system](<https://mauritiusassembly.govmu.org/mauritiusassembly/index.php/download/472/2025/23646/debate-no-16-of-2025-unrevised-tuesday-17-june-2025.pdf>), and that the police had begun to replace it with a new case management system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No count has been found of police stations. Nor has a share entering records in the system. Operating would need more than half of stations entering reports or cases digitally, with a published share or count.

In 2022 a combined crime and gender-based violence record system [was piloted in six districts: Mzimba, Nkhata Bay, Ntchisi, Dowa, Nsanje and Machinga](<https://mptf.undp.org/sites/default/files/documents/2024-08/final_spotlight_initiative_malawi_cumulative_report_revised.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 29 July 2026 the police and UNDP [opened a three-day training on the system in Lilongwe](<https://www.undp.org/malawi/news/dockets-data-malawi-police-and-undp-malawi-advance-digital-transformation-crime-management>). In July 2026 the Crime Management System [was being introduced across stations and formations](<https://www.undp.org/malawi/news/dockets-data-malawi-police-and-undp-malawi-advance-digital-transformation-crime-management>). No source names or counts a station using it, or says whether the 2022 system stayed in use. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

In October 2026 the Acting Inspector-General said the [Force Case Docket Management System](<https://neweralive.na/nampol-pushes-for-digital-investment-ict-overhaul-to-modernise-services/>) is accessible at [all Class A and Class B police stations](<https://neweralive.na/nampol-pushes-for-digital-investment-ict-overhaul-to-modernise-services/>) and [about 90% of Class C stations](<https://neweralive.na/nampol-pushes-for-digital-investment-ict-overhaul-to-modernise-services/>). In the last twelve months, the force said it had [begun an overhaul of the E-Policing System](<https://neweralive.na/nampol-pushes-for-digital-investment-ict-overhaul-to-modernise-services/>). No timetable or funding was given. A 2022 study of stations in the Omusati region found that [officers there record by hand](<https://digital.unam.edu.na/xmlui/handle/11070.1/18365>). No count of stations has been found. Operating would need more than half of stations entering reports or cases digitally, with a published share or count.

EUCAP Sahel Niger reported on 23 May 2019 that the Direction de la Police Technique et Scientifique in Niamey [works the database](<https://trust-fund-for-africa.europa.eu/news/wapis-sipao-un-fichier-de-police-pour-le-niger-2019-05-23_en>), called SIPAO. Cases are [entered by a team of 8 under the director in Niamey](<https://trust-fund-for-africa.europa.eu/news/wapis-sipao-un-fichier-de-police-pour-le-niger-2019-05-23_en>), and more than 8,000 had been entered by then. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing since May 2019 says the system reached stations outside Niamey or still runs, and no count of stations has been found. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

In June 2021 the Ministry of Police Affairs said [statements and reports at stations were written by hand](<https://fmino.gov.ng/enhancing-effective-policing-with-infrastructural-supportas-wapis-database-centre-debuts/>). On 25 September 2025 the Inspector-General [opened nationwide training on the new Criminal Database Systems](<https://nigeriacommunicationsweek.com.ng/2025/09/25/police-launches-database-to-curb-missing-case-files-others>). In the last twelve months, in June 2026, [Gombe State became the first to receive a digital police station](<https://dailytrust.com/gombe-gets-nigerias-first-digital-police-station/>), where case files can be managed digitally on a cloud-based system. No station outside Gombe is shown recording cases digitally. No count of stations using the Criminal Database Systems has been found. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally in some stations outside the capital.

The Rwanda Investigation Bureau's history of 2017 to 2023, published in October 2024, says the [Ministry of Justice manages the Integrated Electronic Case Management System](<https://www.rib.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/RIB/Journey/RIB-The_2017-2023_Journey.pdf>). The bureau [has incorporated the system to process criminal investigation files](<https://www.rib.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/RIB/Journey/RIB-The_2017-2023_Journey.pdf>). Case handling is [digitalised from investigation to final judgment through the system](<https://www.rib.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/RIB/Journey/RIB-The_2017-2023_Journey.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on whether the bureau's stations and posts enter the case file themselves, or on how many do. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

A thesis abstract from Sudan University of Science and Technology, dated 2022, [proposes converting the reports taken in Sudanese police stations to an electronic system](<https://repository.sustech.edu/handle/123456789/27396>). The same abstract [describes the system for reports in police stations as the old paper one](<https://repository.sustech.edu/handle/123456789/27396>). In the last twelve months, police databases were reported in June 2026 as [restored after the war](<https://www.sudaninet.net/78278>). No source found says how stations have recorded reports since 2022, or how many stations use a system. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

No stage is set. The one records tool found, ARHIP, was shown at a design workshop on 2 October 2025. Its technical form is not stated, and its use in the units was still under discussion. In the last twelve months, the Police nationale launched an [online platform for reporting cybercrime](<https://aps.sn/une-plateforme-numerique-de-signalement-des-infractions-cybercriminelles-officiellement-lancee/>) on 12 February 2026, which takes reports from the public. No dated statement says how stations or gendarmerie brigades record today. No training, delivery, plan or finance has been found for ARHIP. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

The Sierra Leone Police's Strategic Development Plan 2025-2029 names [what it calls an e-Case Management System, for case tracking and processing](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2025-04/police_strategy_booklet_29th_jan-2025.pdf>). The plan [lists a transition from a paper-based to a digital records management system among its priorities](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2025-04/police_strategy_booklet_29th_jan-2025.pdf>), on a 2024 baseline. In the last twelve months, a report of 27 July 2026 said the force [handed 39 laptops to Local Unit Commanders for electronic correspondence](<https://thecalabashnewspaper.com/slp-embraces-digital-transformation-with-distribution-of-computers-to-local-unit-commanders/>). It also said stationery would be kept mainly for operational work. No source found shows the planned survey of case management done, or any other step to prepare the system. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

IDLO stated on 19 April 2024 that [the police use paper-based systems](<https://www.idlo.int/sites/default/files/rfp_n-96-2024-som_electronic_case_management_system.pdf>). Its tender is for the first electronic case management system for Somalia's federal justice institutions. [Its first phase covers only the Criminal Investigation Department in Mogadishu](<https://www.idlo.int/sites/default/files/rfp_n-96-2024-som_electronic_case_management_system.pdf>), and nothing was built in April 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether the police enter reports or cases in any system built since the tender, and no station is named as doing so. Preparing would need a system for stations to record reports or cases being prepared or piloted.

[In 2021 UNDP supported a unified case management system in Juba](<https://rolhr.undp.org/annualreport/2021/africa/south-sudan.html>), which serves the courts, the justice ministry and the police service. In the last twelve months, [on 5 December 2025 a UN mission police officer handed a crime management system he had built to the police ICT directorate in Juba](<https://cand.vn/canh-sat-viet-nam-thiet-ke-thanh-cong-he-thong-quan-ly-toi-pham-tai-nam-sudan-post790283.html>). [Bringing it into official nationwide use was still to come](<https://cand.vn/canh-sat-viet-nam-thiet-ke-thanh-cong-he-thong-quan-ly-toi-pham-tai-nam-sudan-post790283.html>). No count of police stations using either Juba system has been found. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

Eswatini's Integrated Electronic Case Management System, IECMS, [is the Ministry of Justice's programme](<https://independentnews.co.sz/22407/news/reps-attend-iecms-training/>), Independent News reported in August 2025. Royal Eswatini Police Service officers [were trained on entering new cases into the system](<https://independentnews.co.sz/22407/news/reps-attend-iecms-training/>) at the ministry's training of trainers that month. At the Mbabane and Manzini One Stop Centres [the police record by hand in occurrence books](<https://www.unicef.org/eswatini/media/2241/file/OSC%20Eswatini%20Evaluation%20Report.pdf.pdf>), UNICEF's evaluators stated in 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No station, region or start date has been found for police entry of cases in the IECMS. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

Winsoft's account of 6 January 2025 says the Seychelles police case app [manages cases from start to finish and is the repository of every case recorded](<https://winsoft-international.com/seychelles-police-department-chooses-the-filemaker-platform-to-aid-fight-against-crime/>). The detective commander of Mont Fleuri station is [quoted by Winsoft, in January 2025, saying all police stations are connected](<https://winsoft-international.com/seychelles-police-department-chooses-the-filemaker-platform-to-aid-fight-against-crime/>). The same account says [the database is bedding in at headquarters in Victoria](<https://winsoft-international.com/seychelles-police-department-chooses-the-filemaker-platform-to-aid-fight-against-crime/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No count of stations, or of the share entering their own records, has been found. Operating would need more than half of stations entering reports or cases digitally, shown by a published share or a count given with its total.

SIPAO, the West African police information system, is [an ECOWAS programme implemented by INTERPOL with European Union funding](<https://togoenlive.tg/sipao-reflexions-a-lome-sur-lappropriation-et-la-perennisation-aux-niveaux-national-et-regional>). It was handed to ECOWAS and the national authorities on 8 April 2025. In the last twelve months, on 14 April 2026 a police divisional commissioner said [the country's commissariats and gendarmerie brigades have SIPAO as a tool](<https://togoenlive.tg/sipao-reflexions-a-lome-sur-lappropriation-et-la-perennisation-aux-niveaux-national-et-regional>). That is a statement of stations equipped, with no count of stations. No source found says whether any station enters reports or cases in it. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

The Minister for Home Affairs told Parliament in May 2024 that the ministry [has installed a digital case file management information system, to be connected with the criminal justice institutions](<https://dailynews.co.tz/state-allocates-40-5bn-for-installation-of-abis-strengthening-ict/>). He said that by April 2024 [the Central Police Stations in 23 regions had been connected](<https://dailynews.co.tz/state-allocates-40-5bn-for-installation-of-abis-strengthening-ict/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing is dated after May 2024. Nothing found says whether a station enters the case file when the case is opened. Nor does any source give the total of stations. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally in some stations outside the capital.

The Uganda Police Force's ICT Directorate [developed the Crime Records Management System itself](<https://upf.go.ug/police-develops-crime-records-management-system/>). In December 2017 the system was [being piloted in ten divisions of Kampala Metropolitan](<https://upf.go.ug/police-develops-crime-records-management-system/>). The Independent reported in 2021 that it had been [upgraded and tested in Kampala, with tests in upcountry stations to follow](<https://www.independent.co.ug/police-upgrades-digital-crime-record-management-system/>). In June 2024 the Electronic Policing Information System was [in its design phase](<https://iacajournal.org/articles/10.36745/ijca.580>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says whether any station outside Kampala Metropolitan enters cases digitally. Establishing would need reports or cases entered digitally, past any pilot, in some stations outside the capital.

The police told Parliament's police committee on 4 May 2021 that the docket system [was in 998 police stations with 159 still to be covered](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-meeting/32761/>), 86.3% of all police stations. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. The Acting Minister's reply of 31 December 2025 says a docket is opened when a complaint is taken. [It is captured on what the police call the Crime Administration System and the Investigate Case Docket Management System](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/35281/>).
